tecnicas.nome_original: SLM4PLC (correctness-by-construction framework: Agentic RAG + enhanced CoT prompting + syntax checking + CbC Debugging Agent)
tecnicas.localizador: Resumo, PDF p. 1; seção IV (Fig. 1, IV.C–IV.E), PDF p. 2–3; Tabelas I e III, PDF p. 4 (páginas sem número impresso)
tecnicas.observacao: Pacote híbrido: quatro agentes (Retrieval, Coding, Syntax-Checking, CbC Debugging) em pipeline fechado → multiagente e decomposicao; prompts estruturados com restrições de compilador, segurança e validação → instrucao e restricoes; CoT com análise de segurança e antecipação de erros → raciocinio; RAG com documentação PLC e exemplos/templates de ST validados → contexto e exemplos; laço com verificação sintática (RuSTy) e verificação formal (nuXmv) com depuração guiada por contraexemplo → feedback. Inclui também ajuste fino QLoRA do Phi-3 (fora do escopo) na linha Phi-3 3.8B (FT). Comparação com 'Naive LLM (Baseline)' nos mesmos modelos (Tabelas I e III) isola o pacote, não um mecanismo; para os modelos sem rótulo (FT) o estudo não declara explicitamente ausência de ajuste fino. O prompt do baseline ingênuo não é descrito, por isso não se identifica o que o pacote acrescenta (mecanismos_acrescentados vazio). A linha 'CbC Debugging Framework' da Tabela II é apresentada como 'The full CbC Debugging Framework', mas o modelo dessa tabela não é informado.

citacoes.trecho: The proposed framework integrates Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Agentic RAG) with structured Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting to reduce reasoning errors, constrain safety-critical logic, and improve grounding in IEC 61131-3 programming patterns.
A lightweight SLM, fine-tuned using QLoRA, serves as the code generation engine.
Existing large-scale language models (LLMs) are too computationally demanding and lack the formal reliability for deployment on typical PLC hardware.
Cloud-based inference introduces additional concerns regarding latency, confidentiality, and predictable scan-cycle execution.
They help close the Computational Cost Gap that prevents larger LLMs like GPT-4 [15] from running on-site.
Reasoning quality is improved through Chain-of-Thought prompting [20] and RAG [24], both of which help reduce code hallucinations.
This combination prevents both syntactic errors and deeper logical flaws such as deadlocks, unsafe interlocks, or liveness violations, providing robust assurance for generated PLC control logic.

Studies also report persistent logical and semantic errors in LLM-generated PLC programs, motivating research into improved prompting, verification-aware workflows, and divide-and-conquer reasoning strategies.
SLM4PLC builds on this line of work by emphasizing lightweight model adaptation and formal assurance relative to a naive LLM baseline.

The system coordinates four agents—Retrieval, Coding, Syntax-Checking, and CbC Debugging—in a closed-loop pipeline that ensures the syntactic validity, logical correctness, and formal verifiability of PLC programs.
Fine-tuning was performed on the Phi-3-Mini-128K-Instruct (3.8B) model using QLoRA on a single NVIDIA GTX 950M GPU.
All samples were validated using the RuSTy ST compiler to ensure syntactic correctness, and organized into three task-oriented sets: Generation, Completion, and Fixing.
As shown in Fig. 2, the coder agent employs an enhanced Chain-of-Thought (CoT) strategy to guide the model through step-by-step reasoning.
This process includes a brief safety analysis to enforce safety constraints (e.g., interlocks and deadlock freedom) and an error anticipation step to identify common logic issues.
CoT is further supported by retriever-supplied code templates from the Agentic RAG module, enabling the model to generate more accurate and consistent Structured Text code.
Additional divide-and-conquer reasoning and hallucination-reduction techniques further enhance reliability.
It leverages Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to ground code generation in curated PLC documentation and validated ST examples, reducing hallucinations.

Structured, domain-aware prompts encode compiler, safety, and validation constraints, and the agent operates in an iterative loop with syntax-checking and debugging components, enabling feedback-driven refinement and producing reliable, verifiable PLC code.
This trace is fed back to the Fixing Agent (the fine-tuned SLM), which is specifically prompted to perform a surgical code refinement [21], [22].

The evaluation validates the framework against key metrics, comparing six SLM configurations: Mistral 7B, CodeLlama 7B [12], Deepseek-Coder 6.7B [13], Qwen2.5-Coder 7B [14], Phi-3 3.8B, and Phi-3-Mini 3.8B (fine-tune).
To evaluate our framework, we constructed a benchmark dataset for generating IEC 61131-3 Structured Text from natural-language specifications and assessing correctness through formal verification.
The benchmark consists of 20 programming tasks with associated LTL specifications: 12 easy tasks with 52 properties and 7 medium tasks with 31 properties.
The Pass@k metric considers a task successful if at least one of the k generated candidates both compiles and satisfies the specified functional requirements.
As shown in Table I, all SLM4PLC variants achieve a perfect 100% first-pass compilation rate for both Easy and Medium tasks.
These results confirm that domain-aligned fine-tuning and structured prompting significantly improve syntactic robustness in IEC 61131-3 Structured Text generation.
On Easy tasks, verifiable rates increase from 50–58.3% under basic prompting to 66.6% when both components are applied.
The full CbC Debugging Framework achieves the highest performance, with a 75% verifiable rate and a 66.6% pass rate on Easy tasks, and a 57.1% verifiable rate with a 42.9% pass rate on Medium tasks.

citacoes.trecho: As shown in Table III, all SLM4PLC models achieve a perfect syntax compilation pass rate of 100%, successfully compiling all generated programs.
The framework attains a maximum verifiable rate of 66.7% and a pass rate of 58.3% with the fine-tuned Phi-3 3.8B model, demonstrating its superior capability in generating formally verifiable code.
No unexpected behavior or conflicting state updates were observed during execution.
SLM4PLC is designed as a fully offline deterministic workflow that aligns with industrial expectations for safety, confidentiality, and predictable behavior.

extracoes.tecnica: SLM4PLC (correctness-by-construction framework: Agentic RAG + enhanced CoT prompting + syntax checking + CbC Debugging Agent)
extracoes.benchmark: Benchmark próprio de IEC 61131-3 ST com especificações LTL, nível Easy
extracoes.metrica: Syntactic Compilation Attempts — 1st Pass (%) (no texto: 'first-pass compilation rate')
extracoes.denominador: Runs: 10 (Naive LLM; 1st Pass 7, 2nd Pass 3) e 12 (SLM4PLC; 1st Pass 12, 2nd Pass 0); o significado de Runs não é definido
extracoes.condicoes: Comparação de pacote: o ganho é do pacote SLM4PLC (agentes, RAG, CoT, verificação sintática e formal), não de um mecanismo. A linha Mistral 7B do SLM4PLC não tem rótulo (FT); o estudo não declara explicitamente se esse modelo foi ajustado. Prompt do baseline ingênuo não descrito. Denominadores diferentes entre as condições (10 vs 12 Runs). Temperatura, número de execuções por tarefa e k não informados. A Tabela III mostra para o mesmo modelo e nível taxas sintáticas de 10/12 (83.3) no Naive LLM e 12/12 (100) no SLM4PLC, com outra métrica (Syntax Rate) e outro denominador.
